attempt_1.root_cause: Duplicate UNIQUE constraint name uq_intelligence_review_items_session_id in app/models/entities.py's IntelligenceReviewItem (two constraints, same auto-generated name since naming convention keys off first column only), causing 3 tables (intelligence_review_items, committee_conflict_declarations, decision_quality_reviews) to fail creation via cascading FK/index errors

schema_apply.fix_applied: Added explicit distinct names to the two UniqueConstraint declarations; regenerated backend/sql/001_initial_schema.sql and PIOS_MVP_PostgreSQL_Schema_v1.4.sql via the existing scripts/export_postgres_ddl.py

attempt_1.root_cause: TimestampMixin.row_version is NOT NULL with only a Python-side SQLAlchemy default=1 (no server_default), so every raw INSERT in the exported seed SQL - which never lists row_version - violated the NOT NULL constraint on the very first statement (organizations), aborting the whole transaction and cascading 'transaction aborted' errors through all 650 remaining statements

seed_apply.fix_applied: Added server_default=text("1") to TimestampMixin.row_version (same pattern already used for created_at/updated_at's server_default=func.now()); regenerated the exported schema files

attempt_1.error: StringDataRightTruncation: value too long for character varying(32)
attempt_1.root_cause: Alembic's default alembic_version.version_num column is VARCHAR(32); 7 of 13 revision id strings exceed 32 characters (up to 42)

alembic_upgrade_head_from_empty_db.fix_applied: migrations/env.py now pre-creates alembic_version with a VARCHAR(255) version_num column before Alembic's own checkfirst=True table creation runs. Does not rename any revision id or alter any migration file's content.

attempt_2.root_cause: 0001_initial creates ALL current Base.metadata tables via create_all() (previously flagged in the engineering audit). Migrations 0002-0010 consistently use raw 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS' SQL, tolerant of that. Migrations 0011-0013 instead use Alembic's structured op.create_table() API (22 tables total), which has no automatic IF NOT EXISTS guard, so they collide with what 0001 already created.

alembic_upgrade_head_from_empty_db.final_status: FAIL - not fixed. Fixing this requires editing migration 0011/0012/0013 content, which is explicitly out of scope per instruction not to alter historical migrations. See blocker_register.json.
alembic_upgrade_head_from_empty_db.conclusion: The Alembic migration chain is NOT currently operational for a fresh installation. This is confirmed, reproducible, and root-caused precisely - not a hypothesis.

before_fix.match_to_expected_baseline: PARTIAL - tables/columns/foreign_keys matched, indexes and constraints did not

verify_post_import_sql.root_cause: The script's own indexes/constraints queries counted different things than the documented baseline comment: pg_indexes includes implicit PK/UNIQUE-backing indexes (92+77=169 extra); information_schema.table_constraints synthesizes one virtual CHECK-type row per NOT NULL column per the SQL standard (973 extra). Not a schema defect.
verify_post_import_sql.fix_applied: Rewrote the indexes query to exclude indexes backing a named constraint, and the constraints/foreign_keys queries to use pg_constraint directly instead of information_schema.table_constraints.

after_fix.match_to_expected_baseline: PASS - exact match on all five metrics

test_suite_against_postgresql.note: First time in this project's available history that the full suite has run against a real PostgreSQL server rather than SQLite. Uses Base.metadata.create_all() (SQLAlchemy Core), not the Alembic migration chain, and not the raw exported seed SQL - a third, independent code path from the two tested above.

phase4_oidc_validation.reason: No Keycloak or other real OIDC provider is installed or running in this environment, and no authorized institutional issuer/tenant exists regardless. Installing a throwaway OIDC provider was out of scope for the same reason as Phase 3.

phase5_migration_integrity_assessment.fresh_install_correctness: FAIL - alembic upgrade head does not complete against an empty database (confirmed above, blocked at revision 0011)
phase5_migration_integrity_assessment.incremental_migration_auditability: COMPROMISED - 0001_initial creates the CURRENT schema via Base.metadata.create_all() rather than a fixed historical snapshot, so the migration history cannot be used to audit what changed at each sprint boundary
phase5_migration_integrity_assessment.historical_reproducibility: NOT POSSIBLE - there is no way to stand up the database as it actually existed after any single historical migration (e.g. 'just after Sprint 5'); running migrations 0001 through any point always yields the current full schema via 0001 alone
safe_forward_only_remediation_recommende: Do not edit 0001_initial.py or any existing migration file.

Add a new migration (e.g. 0014_normalize_fresh_install_guard) that is a genuine no-op against any database that already has the full schema (checks table existence before acting), so both fresh installs and already-migrated databases converge safely - this does not fix historical auditability, only fresh-install correctness.

For migrations 0011-0013 specifically, a new forward migration could wrap equivalent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS logic for those 22 tables so a fresh install can pass through revision 0011 without modifying 0011's original content.

Widening alembic_version.version_num (already applied in migrations/env.py this validation) should be kept regardless of the above, since it is an independent, permanent defect unrelated to the 0001_initial design question.
Longer term and requiring explicit approval: a deliberate 'squash to a real 0001' rewrite, which the task's own rules for this validation pass explicitly forbid without separate authorization.
